svg.title: Proposed standalone Metal network handoff
svg.desc: Management admits exact intent on the hub. One selected cell writes local results reflected by Karmada. Networking owns paths and addresses; Fleet boot owns the admitted response. Disconnect and settlement precede claim disposition and capacity release.
svg.text: Standalone Metal: authority, paths and acknowledged handoff
PROPOSED CONTRACT • no implemented integration or hardware qualification implied
Fleet management
Immutable allocation + admitted operation
Installation, driver, inputs, fence, custody
Verifies evidence before public status
Federation hub
Management-authored exact intent
Karmada delivers to selected cell
Only Karmada reflects results
Selected cell
Local execution + local results only
No project or hub API credentials
No expanded authority during partition
Local result → reflection → management verification
Networking owner: path + address authority
Feasibility ≠ address reservation ≠ programmed attachment
NIC mapping, IPAM, switch, DHCP/RA, routing, isolation
Exact binding revisions + attributable dataplane evidence
Provider-assigned facts are observations, not Datum intent
Fleet boot + scoped proxy: admitted response
Installation-bound script, digest, endpoint and step budget
Every connection/redirect/artifact origin policy checked
Execution owner separately proves stop + local-disk boot
No customer DHCP authority or direct-fetch escape
Release barrier: unknown never becomes free capacity
Close admission → fence old effects → disconnect acknowledgment → coordinator settlement → claim disposition
Networking holds exact assignments; stale detach cannot touch a new binding even if the IP is reused.
Release owner also requires boot/session revocation, installer settlement and provider cleaning evidence.
Commissioning → isolation • Provisioning → stop/revoke/isolate → Customer • Every transition consumes exact owner evidence
